paper_title: Measuring the stability of fundamental constants with a network of clocks
notes: This is a science case paper for the QSNET (A network of clocks for measuring the stability of fundamental constants) project. The paper discusses projected sensitivities to variations of the fine structure constant α and electron-to-proton mass ratio μ using a network of atomic and molecular clocks. While the paper extensively discusses theoretical frameworks for scalar field couplings to electrons and photons (Eqs. 1-2, 15-18), and presents projected sensitivity curves in Figures 5-8, it does NOT present actual measured exclusion limits or new observational data. Instead, it presents: (1) PROJECTED sensitivities for future QSNET measurements (Fig. 5b,c show sensitivity projections for α and μ variations); (2) Comparisons with EXISTING limits from other experiments (Figs. 6-8 show QSNET projections overlaid on existing bounds from clock comparisons, equivalence principle tests, etc.). The paper is fundamentally a proposal/design document for a future experiment, not a report of new measurements. The coupling type ScalarElectron is suggested because the paper discusses scalar field couplings to electron mass (d_me terms in Eqs. 1-2, 17-18) and electron-photon interactions, but no actual numerical coupling limits are extracted as measured data points. The sensitivity curves in Figures 5-8 are projections, not measured bounds. Therefore, extraction_confidence is very low (<0.3) because there are no actual measured exclusion limits to extract, only future projections.
